title: eval-harness: add per-prompt CI hooks and per-prompt histogram metrics for regression gating
author: Aisha Kumar
description: Motivation: make eval-harness CI able to gate regressions at the prompt-set level and provide finer-grained histogram metrics per prompt to help triage quality regressions. This change adds a per-prompt CI hook that runs lightweight evaluations on changed prompt sets, emits per-prompt histograms to our metrics backend, and wires those metrics into the existing regression gating logic. What this PR does: - Introduces ci/hooks/per_prompt_hook.py: a CI entrypoint that detects changed prompt sets, runs the configured evals with a short sample, and emits summary histograms. - Adds metrics/prompt_histograms.py: utilities to bucket and emit prompt-level score distributions (p99/p95/median and histogram bins). - Updates ci/workflows/eval_harness.yml to include a new job (per-prompt-eval) which runs in parallel to the full eval but is lightweight and fast. - Adds tests (tests/eval/test_per_prompt_hooks.py) and docs (docs/eval-harness/ci.md) describing how the per-prompt gating works and how to tune thresholds. - Small integration: registers the new metrics in redwood/observability/metrics_registry.yaml and exposes them to the eval gating service. Checklist: - [x] Add per-prompt CI hook and workflow - [x] Emit histogram metrics and wire to registry - [x] Tests for hook logic and threshold parsing - [x] Docs for maintainers and SREs - [x] Performance: run sampled evals under 90s for typical prompt sets Notes: The description and thresholds are configurable via existing eval-harness config. The hook intentionally runs a small sample (default 50 examples) to keep latency and cost low but still provide signal for regressions. For any prompt sets with non-deterministic evals, the CI will mark the result as flaky and defer to full eval runs. Related: ENG-1287 (per-prompt gating design), SUP-3421 (customer-reported noisy quality regression on a single prompt set).

diff_snippets:
+ def run_per_prompt_hook(changed_prompts):
+     for p in changed_prompts:
+         scores = sample_eval(p, sample_size=config.sample_size)
+         emit_histogram(metric_name=f'eval.prompt.{p}.score', scores=scores)

+ class PromptHistogram:
+     def __init__(self, bins):
+         self.bins = bins
+     def to_metrics(self):
+         return { 'p99': compute_p99(self.bins), 'p95': compute_p95(self.bins), 'median': compute_median(self.bins) }

release_notes: Add per-prompt CI hooks and histogram metrics to eval-harness. Enables faster regression detection on individual prompt sets and provides per-prompt score distributions for triage.
impact_and_rollback: Low-risk: additive CI job and metrics wiring. Rollback: remove new workflow / unregister metrics registry entries. No runtime changes to production inference paths.
testing_and_perf: Lightweight sampled runs default to 50 examples; end-to-end per-prompt job completes under 90s on CI runners in our cloud. Added unit tests covering threshold parsing and flaky detection. Observability: prometheus exporter validates histogram buckets in sandbox environment.
how_to_verify: 1) Open PR that changes a prompt set -> per-prompt CI job should run and post result comment. 2) Check metrics dashboard (Eval -> Per-prompt histograms) for newly emitted metrics. 3) Run tests: pytest tests/eval/test_per_prompt_hooks.py
